**Routing:** Is this about decisionRuntime 'claude-in-session': a thread's Wardens held as background subagents inside its own Claude Code process (InSessionWardens, agent-session ClaudeInSessionDecisions), the setup turn and the foundry-root / foundry-dispatch / foundry-warden tree, the moment / answer / next tools, queued turns and ThreadMeta.setup while it sets up, dispatcher recycle, orphans, perTaskStopAffordance, or the subagent cap raise? Plain jobs: run Wardens without a process per Warden, hold Wardens ready between messages, keep Warden activity from waking the main model.

## Glossary

**claude-in-session**  
The `subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime` value that turns this runtime on; off by default.

**CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS**  
Subagent cap the launch raises (by 76 today) so Wardens don't starve the user's own subagents.

**ClaudeInSessionDecisions**  
agent-session 0.6.6 class that runs the root, dispatcher and Warden tree inside a Claude main session.

**ClaudeSubagentSessions**  
agent-session side-session runtime: a side process per thread with a dispatcher agent and standby moments.

**CodexPrimedSessions**  
One Codex app-server per account with a primed thread per decision role; Codex Wardens stay here.

**fallback to primed**  
A thread whose Warden tree is not running sends its Wardens to primed sessions, as if the setting were off.

**foundry-dispatch**  
A dispatcher generation: a background subagent that starts Warden spares and absorbs their endings.

**foundry-root**  
The never-ending background root agent that starts dispatcher generations.

**foundry-warden**  
The one generic Warden agent definition; each spawn's prompt is pinned to its composed text.

**in-session-wardens**  
This region's class: Wardens held as subagents inside the thread's own Claude Code process.

**IN_SESSION_DECISION_CONTEXT**  
Exported constant of providers/in-session-wardens.ts.

**InSessionWardens**  
Holds each thread's in-session Warden host and routes that thread's Warden calls to it.

**moment / answer / next**  
Foundry's SDK MCP tools: hold for a moment, answer it, fetch the next spares to start.

**orphan**  
A nested agent whose parent ended; its own end would wake the main model, so it is never stopped; past 40 the thread stops serving in-session.

**perTaskStopAffordance**  
`initialize` flag that makes the user's Stop interrupt the main turn without killing background Wardens.

**prestartWardens**  
Pre-starts Wardens on thread start, turn landed and thread-knowledge change.

**queued**  
Turn status for messages typed during setup; sent in order when ready, failed by restart recovery.

**recycle**  
Past 100k tokens of dispatcher context a new generation starts and the old one ends into the root, no main turn.

**SessionBackedProvider.open**  
Opens the thread's session on its first accepted turn, provisionally; relaunches with setup if the turn changes model or launch settings.

**setup turn**  
A hidden Foundry-authored turn (`actor: 'foundry'`, `kind: 'setup'`) that starts the Warden tree.

**spare**  
A started Warden held on `moment`, ready to answer the next trigger.

**ThreadMeta.setup**  
`{ status: starting | ready | degraded, wardens: { expected, held, failed }, runtime }`, streamed on `threads`.

**unsolicited main turn**  
A main-model turn caused by a background task ending; the tree is shaped so there are none.

**warm set**  
Design note, not built: hold only recently routed regions' spares (`warmWardens`) instead of the whole chorus.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The claude-in-session decision runtime (off by default): a thread's Wardens hosted as subagents inside the thread's own Claude Code process, started by a hidden setup turn, held on Foundry's moment tool, and served fresh per call with no main-model turn, so one process serves each thread.

## 2. The domain

With `subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime: 'claude-in-session'`, `InSessionWardens` attaches a host per thread and routes that thread's Warden advice, guard and review calls to it; agent-session's `ClaudeInSessionDecisions` runs the machinery. The thread's session opens on its first accepted turn (`SessionBackedProvider.open`, provisional); turns typed meanwhile wait as `queued`, and `ThreadMeta.setup` streams the "Setting up your thread" status. A Foundry-authored **setup turn** asks the main model to start `foundry-root` in the background; the root never ends and starts dispatcher generations (`foundry-dispatch`), which start Warden spares (`foundry-warden`). Each spare holds `moment`, answers through `answer`, and the dispatcher calls `next` for replacements, all over Foundry's SDK MCP server on the control channel, never vendor hook files. A trigger answers a held spare (or starts a member with the moment inline), and Foundry appends the result itself so NO_COMMENT stays invisible. Agent definitions are generic; each spawn's prompt is pinned to its freshly composed text, so edits reach the next call.

The runtime's rules exist to keep the main model asleep and the user's session intact: always declare `perTaskStopAffordance: true`; keep child frames out of the main turn; recycle a dispatcher past 100k tokens through the root with no main turn; never retire or stop an orphan's members; drain on close and never end the root; raise `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` so the user's own subagents keep their slots; answer the SDK MCP connect before `initialize` returns. A thread whose tree is not running falls back to primed sessions. Codex in-process is not built: Codex Wardens stay on `CodexPrimedSessions`.

Neighbours: the `decision-hosts` region holds the default primed and side-session runtimes (`ClaudePrimedSessions`, `ClaudeSubagentSessions`), budgets and the decision login, and the other decision roles that never run in-session; the `chorus` region holds which Wardens a thread has; the `warden-triggers` region holds when they are asked; the `native-sessions` region holds the session adapters and agent-session's transports; the `threads-journal` region holds the thread tree, subagent child threads and queued turns in the journal. Not here: the structural tool gate and `subagents.native` redirect/observe (`tool-gate-mcp`), and what a session receives each turn (`native-sessions`).

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.1 Spec (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.1 Spec

When a thread opens, Foundry launches every Warden up front. A slower start is fine. The user can type meanwhile: each message waits as a `queued` turn (`pf/persistence/local-session-store.ts` `TurnStatus`) until setup is done. The viewer and the ACP host show *"Setting up your thread; feel free to start typing; we'll tell you when it's ready."*

**Claude.** Foundry sends its own **setup turn** on the main thread's session. It starts one background **Foundry dispatcher** subagent. The dispatcher pre-starts every Warden as its own (nested) subagent, held on Foundry's `moment` tool, the same standby mechanism as agent-session's prestart (`as/claude-subagents.ts`). It works over the control channel, not through vendor hook files. A Warden answers through Foundry's `answer` tool. When every Warden it started has returned, the dispatcher calls `next`, and Foundry answers with the Wardens to start again. So after the setup turn, **no Warden activity ever needs a main-model turn**.

**Codex.** Foundry starts the Warden threads directly (`thread/start`) in the main thread's own `codex app-server`. No setup turn is needed. This depends on per-thread violation handling (C.2 Q6, C.8 question 6).

Either way, the whole tree is **one process per main thread**.

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-2-why-these-mechanisms-the-experiment-2026-10-13 -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.2 Why these mechanisms (the experiment, 2026-10-13) (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.2 Why these mechanisms (the experiment, 2026-10-13)

The scripts are not committed. They were run from the session scratchpad against Claude Code 2.1.296 and codex-cli 0.155.1, driven the way agent-session drives sessions:
- Claude: `--print --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`, an SDK MCP server over the control channel, and a control-channel PreToolUse hook that pins each Warden's prompt, exactly as `as/claude-subagents.ts:861-935`.
- Codex: `codex app-server --listen stdio://`.

All runs were Haiku 5.5 at low effort, about 60 Haiku calls in total, plus a few short Codex calls. The first run went through the cmux `claude` shim and the later ones through the real binary (`~/.local/bin/claude`). The outcomes were the same; the numbers below are from the real binary. RSS is one sample per point, so read it to about ±20 MB.

**Q1. Do background subagents started in a setup turn stay alive after the turn ends? Yes.**
- 3 Wardens started with `run_in_background: true`. The setup turn ended (`result`, "READY") 3.0 s after it was sent, and all 3 were holding `moment` by 3.7 s.
- They were still holding after 60 s and after a later user turn ("PONG"), which ended normally.
- With 10 Wardens behind the dispatcher, all 10 were holding 7.5 s after the setup turn started.

**Q2. Can a later turn hand them input? Yes, but not the way that works for Wardens.**
- **Answering the held `moment` call from Foundry, with no turn at all:** the Warden answered in 1.5–2.8 s.
- **A later main-model turn using `SendMessage`:** this resumed a *finished* background Warden, keeping its earlier conversation, and it answered in about 2.5 s. That makes it a continuing conversation. Wardens must be fresh every call (CLAUDE.md), so this path is out.

**Q3. What does a background Warden finishing do to the main thread? It costs a main-model turn, unless a dispatcher sits in between.**

| Ending of a directly backgrounded Warden | Notification | Unsolicited main-model turns |
|---|---|---|
| Completes normally | `completed` | **1** (the main model narrates the finding, unprompted) |
| Foundry sends `stop_task` after taking its answer | `stopped` | **1** (the main model says "w1 was stopped…") |
| Nested under a background dispatcher, two full rounds of 3 | — (the dispatcher absorbs them) | **0** |

- Every background task ending wakes the main model. With 10 Wardens on every message, on an Opus main thread, that is 10 extra Opus turns per message, and they pollute the main context. A dispatcher in between absorbs the endings.
- Its own context grows by about 400–600 tokens per Warden started: 3,111 → 5,045 → 6,263 tokens over two rounds of 3. So it needs a recycle now and then (C.8, question 3).
- Restarting consumed Wardens through `next` took 2.6 s with no main turn. The main thread's next user turn was unaffected (PONG, 42 tokens of cache write).

**Q4. Interrupts.**
- An interrupt during a main turn spared all held Wardens when the session's `initialize` declared `perTaskStopAffordance: true`.
- Without it, Claude Code's documented behaviour is that "the interrupt kills background tasks" (from the CLI's own control schema). So Foundry must always declare it.

**Q5. Memory (RSS, one process).**

| Setup | Processes | RSS |
|---|---|---|
| Main session, no Wardens | 1 | 243–267 MB |
| + 3 Wardens backgrounded directly | 1 | 273 MB |
| + dispatcher + 3 Wardens held | 1 | 335 MB |
| + dispatcher + 10 Wardens held | 1 | 331 MB |
| After two rounds of use (3) | 1 | 344–363 MB |
| **Today, option (b):** main session + one side session per thread | 2 | ≈260 + 210–320 MB (side session measured 2026-10-12: 210 MB idle, 300–320 MB with 23 subagents) |
| **Before (b):** a primed process per Warden and phase | ~2 per Warden | 130–230 MB each; 25 Wardens ≈ 50 processes, ≈10 GB |

- The dispatcher's first nested subagent costs about +70 MB once. Further held Wardens cost little: 3 versus 10 is within noise.
- **In-session, one main thread with 10 Wardens is about 330 MB in one process, against about 470–580 MB in two processes for option (b).** That makes it roughly 1.5–1.8× denser, and it reaches CLAUDE.md's "one process tree per main thread".
- **[unverified]** RSS with 20+ Wardens, and growth over a long thread.

**Q6. Codex app-server. Sub-agent threads live in the same process, and Foundry can hand them input directly.**
- A setup turn on the main thread spawned 3 sub-agents (`collabAgentToolCall`, `tool: spawnAgent`) in 8.5 s. Each finished its first turn.
- After the main turn ended, `thread/loaded/list` showed all 4 threads loaded.
- `turn/start` straight on a child thread got its answer in 2.0 s, with **0** main-thread turns triggered.
- The `app-server` process itself stayed at 43 MB with 1 thread and with 4. The process tree (~350–480 MB) is the user's own Codex MCP servers, which a Foundry launch disables.
- Child threads are not announced with `thread/started`. Foundry finds them in `collabAgentToolCall.receiverThreadIds`.
- **Conclusion: for Codex, `spawnAgent` and a setup turn add nothing.** Foundry can start Warden threads itself with `thread/start` in the same app-server.
- **But the existing Codex decision host can't simply move in.** `as/codex-primed.ts` runs **one app-server per account** hosting every key's thread (not one per thread). It relies on rules a main thread can't follow:
  - a private `CODEX_HOME` holding only the login;
  - tool features, plugins and MCP disabled;
  - `approval_policy=never`;
  - **recycling the whole process on any violation** (`as/codex-primed.ts:5, 26-30, 84-90`).

  In the main thread's app-server, a recycle would kill the user's thread, and one process has one `CODEX_HOME`. So for Codex, "one process per main thread" means:
  - per-thread violation handling (interrupt and drop the Warden thread, never recycle);
  - per-thread disabling of tools and MCP, which codex-primed already does per thread;
  - accepting the main thread's `CODEX_HOME`.

  C.8 question 6.
- Fresh-per-call is a fork of the primed thread per call, as codex-primed does today.
- **[unverified]** whether the main thread's app-server can host primed Warden threads alongside a running main turn without contention.

#### C.3 What exists, and what moves

| Today | Where | This spec |
|---|---|---|
| `ClaudeSubagentSessions`: one side **process** per thread (more above 12 Wardens). It has a dispatcher agent, a PreToolUse hook that pins inputs, the `moment` standby, settling on task frames, and a rewind after each fan-out. | `as/claude-subagents.ts` (PR #13) | The same machinery, hosted in the main thread's session. The dispatcher becomes a background subagent instead of the session's own agent, and the hook tells the dispatcher's spawns from the main agent's own. |
| `prestartWardens`: pre-start on thread start, turn landed, and thread-knowledge change. | `docs/subscription-decisions.md` (on `feat/warden-side-sessions`) | Unchanged triggers. Thread start now goes through the setup turn. |
| **Rewind.** The side session rewinds its dispatcher after every fan-out (`as/claude-subagents.ts:715-721`). | agent-session | Not possible in-session: rewinding would rewind the user's conversation. The dispatcher's context grows instead, and is recycled (C.8 question 3). |
| **Fixed definitions.** Each role is a `--agents` definition written at launch; a changed definition reaches only the next side session (`as/claude-subagents.ts:410-423, 843-858`). | agent-session | The main session is never relaunched, so a Settings edit or a feedback `apply` would never reach in-session Wardens. That breaks "running threads take edited Warden instructions on their next turn" and FEEDBACK-LOOP L4. **DECIDED (Aron, 2026-10-14): composition.** *"All these things should be compositional."* There is one generic `foundry-warden` definition, with no prompt of its own. Each spare's standby prompt carries that Warden's freshly composed text (the fixed charter, the generic Warden, then this project's instructions for it), pinned by the hook. That text comes from the existing project agents (`projects[id].agents`: standalone, `extends`, `override`) and the composition view. *"Not every generic one runs in every project... there should be the option to inherit this warden or extend this warden specifically to this project."* An edit reaches the next call. It costs per-definition prompt caching; the standby prefix is still cached. **[unverified]** whether Claude Code reloads `--agents` without a restart. |
| **Launch settings.** The side session runs `--no-session-persistence`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `bypassPermissions`, a 24 h `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` and `--setting-sources ""` (`as/claude-subagents.ts:861-897`). | agent-session | None of these can move to the main session. What follows in-session: (1) the 24 h timeout would apply to the user's own MCP tools, so `moment` holds need a per-tool deadline in Foundry's own MCP server instead, **[unverified]** whether a per-server timeout exists; (2) the main session keeps the user's mode and hooks, so Warden subagents run under them, **[unverified]** whether user hooks fire on Warden tool calls; (3) the Warden agent types are advertised to the main model, so the hook denies any `foundry-*` spawn not issued under the dispatcher. |
| SUBAGENTS.md §3(c) `subagents.native = redirect` denies `tool:Agent` / `tool:Task`, and `observe` records every native child with `handoff` rows. | Oracle `docs/foundry/reference/SUBAGENTS.md` | The dispatcher subtree is exempt from both: the gate allows exactly one `foundry-dispatch` spawn in a Foundry setup turn plus spawns issued under it, and observe mode records it as the dispatcher node (C.4), not as observed children. `--disallowedTools Task` can't be used for redirect while in-session Wardens run. |
| agent-session merges child frames into the in-flight parent turn, and child text can overwrite the parent's (SUBAGENTS §2, `as/turn-state.ts:66`). | agent-session | **Prerequisite** (SUBAGENTS §8 step 1): child frames are tagged and kept out of the main turn, or Warden text lands in the user's reply. |
| `CodexPrimedSessions`: one app-server **per account** with a primed thread per role, recycled on any violation. | `as/codex-primed.ts` | The primed threads move into the main thread's app-server, with per-thread violation handling (C.2 Q6). |
| `queued` turn status. | `pf/persistence/local-session-store.ts` | Turns typed during setup wait as `queued`. Restart recovery fails them, as today. |
| Interrupts. | agent-session `initialize` | Declares `perTaskStopAffordance: true`, so the user's Stop never kills Wardens. |

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-4-record-shapes -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.4 Record shapes (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.4 Record shapes

- **`ThreadMeta.setup`**: `{ status: 'starting' | 'ready' | 'degraded'; startedAt; readyAt?; wardens: { expected: n, held: n, failed: string[] }; runtime: 'claude-in-session' | 'codex-in-process' | 'side-session' }`. It streams on `threads`, which drives the "we'll tell you when it's ready" notice.
- **Setup turn**: a Foundry-authored turn, `actor: 'foundry'`, `kind: 'setup'`. The viewer hides it from the transcript. It is journaled and archived like any turn, so the tree shows the dispatcher as a child node of the root (spec A).
- **Dispatcher node**: a child node, `spawn.via = 'foundry-dispatch'`, with `depth` 1. Each Warden spare is a child of it (`depth` 2) in the journal. In Archive, Warden spares are **not** sessions; their calls are reduced entries (spec A). The dispatcher node is archived as metadata only.
- **Per Warden call** (unchanged from spec A/B): the reduced entry, plus `servedBy: {runtime, taskId}` for debugging.

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-5-who-does-what-and-when -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.5 Who does what, and when (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.5 Who does what, and when

1. **Thread opens.**
   - Foundry starts the main session (one Claude CLI or one Codex app-server), with `perTaskStopAffordance: true` and Foundry's SDK MCP server (`moment`, `answer`, `next`).
   - `ThreadMeta.setup.status = 'starting'`.
2. **Setup.**
   - Claude: Foundry sends the setup turn. The main model starts `foundry-dispatch` in the background and replies READY. The dispatcher calls `next`, and Foundry returns the thread's Wardens (its project's chorus). The dispatcher starts every Warden in one message. Each Warden calls `moment` and is held.
   - Codex: Foundry calls `thread/start` plus a primer for each Warden in the same app-server.
3. **Ready.** When every Warden is held, or a 30 s setup deadline passes, the status becomes `ready` (or `degraded`, listing those that failed). Queued turns are sent in order.
4. **A trigger** (user message, action, spawn, ask, hand-back, landed). Foundry answers each relevant held `moment` with the moment. Each Warden answers through `answer`, and Foundry appends the result ("this Warden chimed in with…"). Wardens with no matching spare are started through `next` and answer as they start.
5. **Replenish.** When a fan-out's Wardens have all returned, the dispatcher calls `next`. Foundry returns the spares to start again, carrying the thread's new standby context.
6. **Recycle.** When the dispatcher's own context passes a bound, Foundry starts a fresh dispatcher and retires the old one. See C.8 question 3 for how to do that without a main turn.
7. **Close.** `stop_task` for the dispatcher, then the session ends. Once the thread is closing, the main model's narration of that ending does not matter.

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-7-original-intent -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.7 Original intent (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.7 Original intent

Aron, 2026-10-12, 19:46: *"We should figure out: when a thread starts maybe there's a hook that we can deploy to call all those agents, right? Sure it'll take a little bit longer to start up. It's fine, right? Or we could start and we can say, 'Okay we're setting up your thing. Feel free to start typing. We'll get a message when it's all set up.'"*

At 19:44: *"Ideally all of that operates within the main thread's context. Every main thread is an app, as it were, or a session, for Claude or for Codex, and that way memory won't get too crazy. You can still run many sessions at once. Otherwise we're going to have major, major memory problems."*

At 15:36: *"When you start a new thread, start all of them. When you get a message back, start all of them, right? Update all of them."* At 15:01: *"We should do both Codex and Claude Code supported like this."* And on hooks, 2026-10-11: *"i dont like running via claude hooks. thats not agnostic"*. The setup turn and the control-channel tools are Foundry's own harness, not vendor hook files.

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-8-open-questions -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.8 Open questions (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.8 Open questions

**Defaults taken (coordinator, 2026-10-15), as proposed below:**
- (1) the setup turn is hidden from the viewer and the ACP transcript;
- (2) it ships as `decisionRuntime: 'claude-in-session'` next to the existing runtime, and both are measured;
- (3) a dispatcher recycles without any main turn: the depth-3 option proved out cheaply (§C.9);
- (4) Foundry keeps its own "this Warden chimed in with…" append.
- Codex questions 5 and 6 are out of scope: Codex Wardens stay on the per-account decision app-server (already bounded).

1. **Setup-turn visibility.** The setup turn costs the main context about 2k tokens once per thread (measured: 1,979 cache-write tokens and 134 output). Should it be hidden from the viewer and ACP transcript (proposed), or shown as a "Foundry set up N Wardens" line?
2. **How far to go in-session.** Moving Claude Wardens from the side session into the main session trades 1 process for:
   - a dispatcher that lives in the user's session, so the main model sees one background agent;
   - the main thread's model serving the setup turn.

   Ship it as `decisionRuntime: 'claude-in-session'` next to option (b), measure both on real threads, then pick a default?
3. **Recycling the dispatcher without a main turn.** Ending or stopping a background dispatcher wakes the main model once (Q3).
   - Option: a depth-1 root that never ends and runs dispatcher *generations* as foreground children, so a retired generation ends into the root and not the main thread. **[unverified]**: needs depth-3 nesting.
   - Option: accept one main turn per recycle, at about every 100k dispatcher tokens (about 20 fan-outs of 10).
4. **Warden output to the main thread.** Today Foundry appends "this Warden chimed in with…" to the main thread's message. In-session, the main model could see it some other way, but Foundry's own append keeps it controlled and keeps `NO_COMMENT` invisible. Keep it (proposed)?
5. **Codex sub-agent threads or Foundry threads?** The experiment shows Foundry-started threads in the same app-server are enough. Is there any reason to prefer Codex's own `spawnAgent`, for example so the Codex UI shows the Wardens?
6. **Codex in the main app-server:** accept the main thread's `CODEX_HOME` and per-thread violation handling (C.2 Q6), or keep Codex Wardens on the per-account decision app-server? Keeping them gives one Codex decision process per account, not per thread, which is already bounded.
7. **DECIDED: generic definition plus composition** (see C.3, fixed definitions).

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-9-as-built-2026-10-15 -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.9 As built (2026-10-15) (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.9 As built (2026-10-15)

Built for Claude behind `subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime: 'claude-in-session'`, **off by default**. agent-session 0.6.6 (`ClaudeInSessionDecisions`), Foundry (`providers/in-session-wardens.ts`).

**Shape.**
- **Setup.** The thread's session opens when its first turn is accepted, through `SessionBackedProvider.open`.
  - The open is provisional: if the first turn asks for another model or launch settings, the session relaunches, and the setup with it.
  - Its first turn delivers every standing part, since the session starts with no base context.
  - An internal setup turn asks the main model to start `foundry-root` in the background. The turn waits `queued` meanwhile. `ThreadMeta.setup` streams on `threads`, the viewer shows a banner, and foundry-acp shows "Setting up your thread…" and then "Your thread is ready."
- **The tree.** Three levels deep, all agents in the background, all through the host's `next` tool:
  - the root never ends;
  - it starts dispatcher generations (`foundry-dispatch`);
  - they start Wardens (`foundry-warden`).
  - Agent definitions are generic. Each spawn's prompt is pinned by the session's PreToolUse callback to the composed charter, instructions, domain knowledge and thread understanding.
- **Calls.** A Warden holds `moment` and answers through `answer`.
  - Advice, guard and review calls go to a held spare, or, with no spare, start a member with the moment inline.
  - These calls take none of the shared decision slots.
  - Other decision roles stay on primed sessions.
  - A thread whose tree is not running falls back to primed sessions.
- **Recycle (C.8 question 3).** Past 100k tokens of dispatcher context, a new generation starts. The old one's spares are retired as their replacements hold, and it ends into the root once empty, with no main turn.
- **Orphans.** A nested agent whose parent has ended reports its own end, whether completed or stopped, to the main thread, which wakes the main model (verified live).
  - This was the cause of the unprompted main turns first seen at 5 threads (24, 43, 3 and 25 per thread), when dispatchers ended under load.
  - Members of a dispatcher that ended unasked are therefore never retired or stopped, and an orphan's `answer` call is held for the session's life.
  - Past 40 orphans the thread stops serving in-session.
  - A root that dies is set up again at most twice per session; each setup is a main turn.
- **Close.** Members and dispatchers are drained; the root is never ended.
- **Subagents.** Their own Wardens are parked (§C.10). In this runtime only, the main thread's subagents' tool calls are guarded from the main thread's Wardens, and the rows are journalled on the subagent's node.
- **Launch.**
  - Claude Code runs 20 subagents at once by default, so the launch raises `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` by 76 on top of the user's own cap.
  - The SDK MCP server is declared in `initialize` (no extra `--mcp-config`) and answers its connect before `initialize` returns. An unanswered connect cost a 30 s retry, which was the first build's ~28 s stall.

**Measured on this machine** (Claude Code 2.1.300):
- Setup: 23 synthetic Wardens with ~12 KB of composed context each, an Opus main thread, the user's own settings and MCP servers.
- Fan-outs: three full fan-outs of every Warden at once in all threads, plus one while a subagent ran in each main thread.
- Memory: the RSS of every process tree involved.

| Threads | Runtime | Setup to all held (from root start) | Fan-out p50 / p95 | Failures | Memory idle → after fan-outs (subagent running) | Processes | Unprompted main turns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | in-session | 19.6 s (16.4 s) | 1.9 s / 5.5 s | 0 | 0.6 → 1.3 GB (0.7 GB) | 1 | 0 |
| 3 | in-session | 20–24 s (15–19 s) | 4.2 s / 4.6 s | 0 | 1.7 → 3.0 GB (2.0 GB) | 3 | 0 |
| 5 | in-session | 17–19 s (13–14 s) | 4.4 s / 7.7 s | 69 of 345, all one thread (rerun: 0) | 2.5 → 2.3 GB (2.4 GB) | 5 | 0 |
| 1 | primed (today) | none; Wardens prime on first use | warm 3.2 s / 4.6 s; cold 10.9 / 18.9 s | 0 | 0.6 → 4.0 GB (5.4 GB) | 136 | 0 |
| 3 | primed | — | warm 13.8 s / 21.6 s | 46 of 207 | 1.7 → 14.8 GB (14.3 GB) | 416 | 0 |
| 5 | primed | — | warm 5.2 s / 15.9 s; cold 20.9 / 27.8 s | 206 of 345 | 2.9 → 9.5 GB (10.3 GB) | 523 | 0 |

- **Load and timing.** Load averages were 15–55 for the in-session runs and 40–90 for the primed ones (the machine is shared and was heavily loaded earlier in the day).
- **5-thread outliers.** One in-session run at 5 threads had a thread whose dispatcher never started: 69 failures, none in a rerun. Two fixes followed: a skipped dispatcher is re-issued, and a thread without a running dispatcher falls back to primed sessions.
- **Fan-out during a subagent:** p50 2.0–3.6 s, p95 3.1–5.0 s.
- **CPU stress.** Under artificial CPU load (load average 266), 5 in-session threads had 0 failures and 0 main-model wakes.
- **Earlier build.** Before the connect fix, setup took 47–54 s.
- **[unverified]:**
  - an end-to-end run through a Foundry daemon with a live chorus (the numbers above drive agent-session directly);
  - growth over a long thread;
  - user hooks firing on Warden tool calls.

**Deviations from §C.4–C.5:**
- The setup turn is not journalled as a turn: it has no admission, and `ThreadMeta.setup` records it.
- No dispatcher or spare nodes are journalled, and calls carry no `servedBy`.
- Close uses STOP through `next` and drains; it never uses `stop_task`.
- A degraded setup is never upgraded to `ready` later.
- Codex in-process is not built (C.8 question 6).

<!-- unit doc:docs/THREAD-TREE.md#c-10-next-a-warm-set-of-concept-region-wardens-design-note-not-built -->
**Source:** `docs/THREAD-TREE.md` § C.10 Next: a warm set of concept-region Wardens (design note, not built) (in "Thread tree: stitching, composition audit, start-up")

#### C.10 Next: a warm set of concept-region Wardens (design note, not built)

Wardens are now built per concept region (the 23 fixed, hand-named Wardens were retired 2026-10-17; plan step 8, "T7 warm set"). A project has many more Wardens than a thread can hold, so the main thread could keep a **warm set**, not the whole chorus. (Since 2026-10-15 v1 asks every region every time, so this note is shelved with routing.)

- **What is warm.** The regions routed for the thread's recent moments (R1), kept by recency (LRU), bounded by `warmWardens` (proposed 6–8). `prestart` already takes the Wardens as a list: the warm set is just a shorter, changing list. A region leaving it has its spare retired normally (it ends into its dispatcher, so no main turn). A region joining it starts a spare.
- **Slots.** Claude Code runs 20 subagents per session by default, and the main thread's own subagents count against the same cap. In-session use is: root + 1–2 dispatchers + the warm set + a replacement while a used spare finishes (up to 2 × warm set). With a warm set of 8 that is at most about 20, so instead of today's flat `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=96`, the launch should raise the cap by exactly that: the user's own cap (default 20) plus `2 + 2 × warmWardens`. The main thread's own subagents then keep all of their slots.
- **Cold regions.** A routed region outside the warm set starts its member with the moment inline (the existing direct path, 2–4 s at normal load, measured by its prime `cold`), then joins the warm set.
- **Orphans.** A smaller warm set also bounds the cost of a dispatcher dying (§C.9): at most a warm set's worth of orphans per dead generation, against `maxOrphans`.
- **Subagents' own Wardens stay parked.** Subagents get no warm set of their own. In the `claude-in-session` runtime their tool calls are guarded from the main thread's set (§C.9) and this is not extended. The handoff trigger (plan step 10) uses the main thread's warm set to brief a subagent at spawn.
- **Open:** the warm-set size, from the R1 re-test (how many regions a moment routes to at k = 1, 2, 4); whether review calls (post-turn) should take warm spares or always start cold.

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#wardens-in-the-thread-s-own-process-claude-in-session -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Wardens in the thread's own process (`claude-in-session`) (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Wardens in the thread's own process (`claude-in-session`)

Off by default (docs/THREAD-TREE.md spec C; numbers in §C.9). With `decisionRuntime: "claude-in-session"`:

- **One process per thread.** Each executor session hosts its thread's Wardens through agent-session's `ClaudeInSessionDecisions`. The thread's session opens when its first turn is accepted; the turn waits `queued` while an internal setup turn starts the Warden tree, and `ThreadMeta.setup` drives "Setting up your thread" in the viewer and in foundry-acp.
- **What runs there.** Warden advice, guard and review calls. Other decision roles (Cartographer, classifiers, routers, naming, feedback) stay on primed sessions. In-session calls take none of the `maxConcurrent` slots.
- **Login.** In-session Wardens run on the thread's own login (and its Kingdom capacity pool), not on the decision profile.
- **Fallback.** A thread whose Warden tree is not running (setup failed, or too many orphaned members) sends its Wardens to primed sessions, as if the setting were off.
- **Subagents.** In this runtime only, the main thread's subagents' tool calls get the root thread's guard Wardens, journalled on the subagent's node.

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (extracted from the code through the repo's Atlas map, described by a model). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `in-session-wardens`
- **InSessionWardens** `packages/foundry/src/providers/in-session-wardens.ts#InSessionWardens` [primitive] hold each thread's in-session Warden host and route that thread's Warden calls to it Use: new InSessionWardens() // attach a host per thread id before its executor session starts
